prior_state.what_prior_runs_audited: G-COST-3 (2026-11-25 10:11Z) and G-COST-4 (14:37Z) were both recast to ILL-POSED. Neither touched G-COST-1. Its 20.002 bp figure was repeatedly cited as the real, measured cost wall that the whole-programme KILL rests on.

committed_g_cost_1.evidence_string: median realised fill cost 20.002 bp over 36 live snapshots at Binance spot BTC/USDT; KILLS the 8.0 bp cost assumption

finding.headline: G-COST-1's '20.002 bp measured cost wall' is 99.99 percent a hardcoded ASSUMED 10 bp/side taker fee; only 0.002 bp is measured top-of-book spread. The gate is a fee-schedule test, not a measured market fill, and its 8 bp kill wall sits below the 20 bp mandatory round-turn fee so PASS is impossible on this venue by construction.

defects.detail: The fee was NOT fetched. fetch_taker_fee_bps calls the public fee endpoint, which returns nothing without auth, and falls back to a hardcoded 10.0 bp/side (code line ~82). The committed artifact records fee_source = 'published schedule assumed'. So of the 20.002 bp, 20.0 bp is the ASSUMED round-turn fee (2 x 10.0) and only 0.002 bp is measured spread. The number is presented and carried as a measured 'realised fill cost'; it is almost entirely an assumption.

The kill wall is 8.0 bp; the mandatory round-turn fee alone is 20.0 bp on any venue charging >= 4 bp/side. PASS is therefore impossible by construction on this venue: the gate tests the published fee schedule, not any market property. This is the exact vacuity already retired for G-COST-3 (whose [19,24.21] band forced PASS by construction) - here it forces a KILL. The programme retired the PASS-forcing gate but left the KILL-forcing twin standing and labelled it a measurement.

Output said '36 live fills' and '15m horizon'. No orders are sent: it reads the top-of-book 36 times ~0.6s apart (~22s total), so these are 36 quotes in one ~22-second snapshot, not fills, and no 15m holding period is ever measured. At the 14:37Z run min=max=median=20.002 -> the 36 samples carried no measurable variance at all (the entire cost was the flat assumed fee + a 1-cent spread).

spread_immateriality_proof.single_snapshot_spread_variance_note: G-COST-3's single-snapshot spread read was 0.6254 bp at 14:37Z but 0.0017 bp at 15:46Z on the same instrument/venue, a transient wide-book moment. Spread reads vary by up to ~0.6 bp between snapshots; either way the spread is <1 bp and immaterial next to the 20 bp fee.

Replace the false 'live fills / 15m horizon' labels with '36 top-of-book quote snapshots ~0.6s apart (~22s); no holding period measured'.

Add verdict_basis naming the KILL as a fee-schedule KILL, not a measured-fill KILL.
fix.verdict_and_gate_unchanged: verdict stays KILL; threshold stays 8.0 bp; the fee fallback stays 10.0 bp/side; overall stays KILL; CI still exits 1. Nothing was lowered.
fix.not_a_weakening: This is the OPPOSITE of lowering a gate. G-COST-3 was retired to ILL-POSED because retiring it lost nothing (the '1D cost premium' quantity does not exist). G-COST-1 encodes a REAL economic fact - a retail taker pays 2 x taker fee per round turn (~20 bp on Binance VIP0 spot), which exceeds the 8 bp edge budget - so the KILL is KEPT. Only the misrepresentation (an assumed fee dressed as a measured fill cost) is corrected. Retiring G-COST-1 to ILL-POSED would have removed the only live KILL and passed candidates; that was deliberately NOT done.

residual_assumption.basis: Binance spot VIP0 published taker fee 0.1% = 10 bp/side (maker = taker at VIP0). The assumption is correct for a retail taker but is NOT measured here and could differ for maker orders, BNB-fee discounts, higher VIP tiers, or another venue. Unmeasured beyond the published Schedule.
residual_assumption.what_would_measure_it: send a live order and read the actual fill vs mid (requires an API key and an account; out of scope for this keyless proof harness).
